name: Autosomal Recessive Hereditary Demyelinating Motor and Sensory Neuropathy
aliases: AR Hereditary Motor and Sensory Neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Electrophysiological Criteria for Hereditary Motor and Sensory Neuropathy

criteria.description: Progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy with sensory loss
Nerve conduction studies showing demyelinating neuropathy with reduced conduction velocities
Identification of pathogenic biallelic mutations in genes associated with autosomal recessive demyelinating neuropathy
Consistent autosomal recessive inheritance pattern or consanguinity
Histopathological evidence of demyelination and onion bulb formations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive distal motor and sensory neuropathy with electrophysiological evidence of demyelination plus identification of biallelic pathogenic mutations in relevant genes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation is essential for definitive diagnosis; nerve biopsy is rarely required.

searchTerms: weakness and muscle loss in hands and feet
loss of strength in fingers and toes
reduced feeling in hands and feet
loss of sensation in fingers and toes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes

common.symptomName: Steppage gait due to foot drop
searchTerms: steppage gait due to foot drop

common.symptomName: Numbness and paresthesia in hands and feet
searchTerms: tingling and numbness in hands and feet
low muscle tone in hands and feet
floppy muscles in arms and legs
balance issues due to sensory loss
difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness
problems with facial and head nerves
nerve issues affecting face and head

laboratory: Elevated cerebrospinal fluid protein with normal cell count (albuminocytologic dissociation) in some cases
imaging: MRI may show muscle atrophy and fatty infiltration in distal limb muscles
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in genes such as GDAP1, MTMR2, or SH3TC2
other: Nerve biopsy showing segmental demyelination and onion bulb formations

distinguishingFeatures: Earlier onset with more uniform demyelination
Transient episodes triggered by pressure or trauma

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness over weeks
Bulbar symptoms such as dysphagia or dysarthria
references: Pareyson D, Marchesi C. Diagnosis, natural history, and management of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Lancet Neurol. 2009;8(7):654-667.
